Though the matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 16.07.2020 passed in MVC No.313/2016 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Koppal (for short, 'Tribunal'), seeking enhancement of compensation as well as requesting to hold contributory negligence at higher side on the driver of KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-37/F-264.
3.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Koppal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.

4. Brief facts of the case are that on 31.12.2014 at about 05.10 p.m., on N.H-63, Gadag-Hospet road,
near LIC NC: 2025:KHC-D:8557 HC-KAR office, Koppal, the claimant was proceeding from Ashoka circle to new bus stand in the auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-20/A-3404.
At that time, a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-37/F-264 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the said auto rickshaw and caused accident.
Due to which, the claimant sustained injuries.
Hence, filed claim petition seeking compensation.

The accident is caused between the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-37/F-264 and auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-20/A-3404.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:
Sl . Heads. Amount in
No. (Rs.)

1. Loss of income. 1,15,200/-
 2. Medical expenses including food, 1,00,000/-
 nourishment, travelling etc.
 3.
Future medical expenses.

50,000/-
 4. Pain and sufferings.

50,000/-
 5. Loss of amenities in life.

The Tribunal has held that the driver of KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-37/F-264 has contributed 40% towards rash and negligence driving of vehicle and 60% towards driver of auto rickshaw bearing registration No.KA-20/A-3404.
Upon considering the evidence on record, it is adduced in the evidence that, the driver of auto rickshaw has hit the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-37/F-264 and then hit to road divider.

The Tribunal has assessed the evidence correctly,
which needs no interference of this Court.

The Tribunal has apportioned rash and negligence at 40%
to the driver of KSRTC bus, 30% to the driver of auto rickshaw and 30% to the owner of auto rickshaw, since the owner has vicariously liable for enact done by its employee.

Therefore, the owner alone is liable to pay compensation at 60%.
7.
Though the claimant has stated that he has suffered fractured injuries, but there is no medical evidence on record to prove the fractured injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
The Wound Certificate (Ex.P5) reveals that the claimant has suffered simple injures.

The Discharge Summary (Ex.P8) and other medical documentary evidence proved that NC: 2025:KHC-D:8557 HC-KAR the claimant has suffered degloving injury of right thigh with raw surface with HIV positive status.
Therefore, whatever functional disability suffered by the claimant is less than 10%.
The appellant/claimant was aged 14 years old at the time of accident.

Hence, keeping in mind the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager,
National Insurance Company Limited & Another1, this Court holds that the appellant/claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of pain and suffering, loss of earning capacity and loss of amenities etc.

Therefore, whatever compensation awarded by the Tribunal, is found to be just and proper, which needs no interference.
